description: Generate error codes and error classes following naming conventions. Enforces semantic error names (ERR_{DOMAIN}_{REASON}) and correct HTTP mappings at creation time.
context: Use when creating any new error condition or exception class
checklist: 1. IDENTIFY DOMAIN AND REASON: Determine the error domain (USER, PRODUCT, ORDER, PAYMENT, AUTH, VALIDATION, SYSTEM). Refer to .ai/error-codes.md for registry.
2. SELECT REASON: Choose reason from registry (NOT_FOUND, INVALID, ALREADY_EXISTS, UNAUTHORIZED, DECLINED, etc.). Domain/reason pair must not already exist.
3. DETERMINE HTTP STATUS: Look up standard HTTP mapping. Example: INVALID → 400, NOT_FOUND → 404, ALREADY_EXISTS → 409, UNAUTHORIZED → 403.
4. GENERATE ERROR CODE: Generate code following ERR_{DOMAIN}_{REASON} pattern. Example: ERR_USER_NOT_FOUND, ERR_PAYMENT_DECLINED
5. CHECK FOR DUPLICATES: Verify the error code doesn't already exist. Command: python api/error_generator.py --check-exists ERR_USER_NOT_FOUND
6. CREATE ERROR CLASS: Generate error class with code, domain, reason, message, details, HTTP status.
7. FOLLOW RESPONSE FORMAT: Error responses must include: code, domain, reason, message, details, timestamp, trace_id (from standard envelope)
8. TEST ERROR PATH: Verify error is thrown in correct conditions and includes all required fields.
9. VALIDATE CONSISTENCY: Run error_validator.py to check all errors in codebase use registered codes.
10. SCAN FOR ERRORS: Run error_discovery.py to find all error codes in use and verify they're registered.
11. REPORT SUCCESS: Confirm error code generated, HTTP status correct, error class created, validation passed
configuration: response_format: {code, domain, reason, message, details, timestamp, trace_id}
